messages:
carmen: Quick follow-up from yesterday's quant-attn workshop — wanted to capture a few unresolved decisions about dequant fusion and kernel boundaries. TL;DR: we need a minimal ABI for fused-dequant-attn that supports mixed dtypes + graceful fallback.
alice: agree. main tradeoff we discussed: expose a single fused op that assumes pre-packed QKV (int8/fp8) vs keep smaller ops (dequant -> pack -> attn). Single op better perf, but harder to test + less modular.
ben: perf numbers from my microbench: fused op gives ~1.6x throughput on A100 when sequence <= 512 and int8 path used. but FP8 had divergent requant paths, so kernel complexity spiked.
carmen: @ben can you drop the microbench command/snippet? good for the RFC.
ben: sure — snippet used: ```bash
python bench_attn.py --model=llama-7b --dtype=int8 --seq-len=512 --batch=8 --prefetch=kv
``` output: `throughput: 1260 toks/s` for fused, `760 toks/s` for dequant+attn separate.
alice: two interface proposals we sketched:
1) fused_op(qkv_ptr, layout_tag, scale_ptr, out_ptr, flags) -> runtime handles layout + cache
2) small_ops: dequant(qkv_int, scale)->qkv_fp; attn(qkv_fp, kv_cache) -> out
Option 1 needs ABI stability across hardware/compiler variants.
dave: note about KV cache: fused op should allow passing an optional KV cache handle to avoid copies. If we force returning full fp outputs, we lose benefit.
eva: about numeric safety — FP8->FP32 dequant can blow up when ranges are bad; we need a per-tensor clip or validation mode. suggest a `safety_mode` flag: `clip`, `panic`, `rescale`.
alice: +1 to safety_mode. Also add an orthogonal `stats_ptr` to record min/max per-tensor for offline calibration.
ben: concern: adding flags and stats_ptr increases calling overhead; but we can make them optional (nullable). for hot path, JITs will inline.
infra-bot: deploy:kernel-lab -> tests/fused-dequant-attn smoke on staging completed (5/5)
carmen: action items:
- ben: land microbench + add CSV perf outputs to RFC (due EOD Tue)
- alice: draft ABI section with optional kv_handle, flags, stats_ptr (due Thu)
- dave: prototype kv_handle fastpath that maps without copy (POC by next week)
- eva: propose safety_mode semantics and default (clip to 8-bit range?)
alice: one more design note — we should avoid embedding requantization inside fused attention. let fused op produce fp32 outputs and offer a separate `requantize(out_fp, target_dtype)` to keep responsibilities clear.
ben: agreeing with alice: separate requantization gives more reuse and simpler testing. but keep a thin combined helper for customers that want end-to-end int8 outputs.
carmen: ok this thread captured it. if nobody objects I'll fold into the RFC draft tonight and ping for review. :thumbsup:
